scope: Proposition 4.4 (Detection by a unit symbol) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For either coefficient source, A(D) = 1 implies the prescribed analytic order: zero in the even case and one in the odd case. At every such index, v(L(h)) ≤ 2w(D) + C in the even case, (4.13) j(PD) ≤ w(D) + C in the odd case, (4.14) s(h) ≤ C, dimF2 Sel2(E(h) /Q) ≤ C. (4.15) The constants are fixed after choosing the original curve, filter, coefficient normalization and genus partner. For the odd source they are independent of the detecting prime and the working precision, and of the number and size of active primes. Statements about its symbols are used through finite realizations as in Lemma 4.3.
